title: Normalized root and tensor foundations for coordinate adjunctions
statement: Fix distinct primes ell and p, a characteristic-p field k and finite E/Q_ell. For every coefficient base b, operations o, section coordinates q and strict Tate family w, the following data exist. On every separated finite-type k-base there are normalized P1 presentations in b,o, root-projection Kummer line isomorphisms, signed tensor-shift comparisons, line products and pullback comparisons normalized on degree zero, roots and higher pure tensors [def-sp-coordinate-right-comparisons, def-sp-coordinate-tate-tensor-comparisons]. Their affine restrictions and uniform inputs lie in the P1 and chart domains [lem-sp-tower-chart-admissibility, det-sp-tower-p1-adjunction]. The explicit stepComponent is natural and gives the successor right-functor isomorphism; normalized ordinary identity pullback and coefficient unit give its zero-dimensional starting isomorphism. The displayed chart right functor preserves the unnormalized uniform constructible finite-Tor domain. No affine, projection or chart adjunction, nor compatibility with finite adjunctions, is asserted.

source.place: Local pairs and Levels; explicit categorical details of the original coordinate argument

proof.text:
Invertibility of ell on every finite-type k-scheme follows from ell ≠ p.
Use the common base and operations in the projective-line presentation, its trace
and diagonal, then apply the projective-line adjunction theorem. Chart admissibility
places uniform constructible objects and their open extensions in its domain.
At level n, use Base.ideals to replace ell^(n+1) by uniformizer^(e*(n+1)).
The root projection identifies the quotient line with the finite Kummer tensor;
restriction of roots fixes its inverse-image comparison. The identity
p_(n+2)(x)^ell = p_(n+1)(x) proves compatibility with strict transitions.
Multiply these ordinary line systems on pure tensors, where associativity and
scalar multiplication give the displayed equations. Their finite lines are flat,
so the degree-zero complexes are K-flat and their ordinary products derive to
isomorphisms. Descend the signed total-complex shift maps on K-flat representatives.
Combine pullback composition, the tensor associator, line multiplication and shift
addition to obtain step with exactly stepComponent as its component. In degree
zero use ordinary identity pullback, the coefficient unit and shift zero; these
natural identifications give zero and its stated component formula.
